newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends mixed, weather forecasts underpin.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends mixed, weather forecasts underpin.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended mixed after a mostly choppy session, with deferred contracts gaining on jitters over forecasts for cold weather next week in the U.S. High Plains, traders said.
"Export optimism kept CBOT wheat firm relative to us, and worries about next week's weather kept our deferred months firm relative to the nearbys," a KCBT trader said.

Traders said there were concerns that the cold weather might damage to newly emerged wheat, especially after this week's mild weather. But agronomists told Reuters Friday that they expected the cold to have little impact, particularly if snow falls and insulates the plants from the low temperatures.
KCBT December wheat weakened in late liquidation amid thin volumes. The most recent data showed open interest in the December contract down to 3.66 million bushels.
KCBT wheat closed 9-1/2 cents per bushel lower to 2-1/2 cents higher, with December down 9-1/2 cents at $4.42-1/2. March shed 3/4 cent to close at $4.04-3/4.

Benson-Quinn was a featured player, selling one million March bushels and buying 700,000 March, traders said. LFG bought 1.1 million March and FIMAT bought one million March. CIS bull-spread 700,000 May/March at 29 to 30 cents.
